minutes.headline: Task force heard how to line up the next Green Communities grant round: energy audits first, then a project list.
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force met with town and school facilities staff to plan the next Green Communities grant round, expected next spring. Discussion centred on needing energy audits and a feasibility study with a short payback, a list of facilities projects (heat pumps, boilers, rooftop units), and a state technical assistance grant due in November. The group then reviewed the nearly finished LED street light project and talked about community outreach. No formal votes were recorded, apart from a closing motion whose result is not audible.

votes.motion: A motion was called at the end of the meeting (apparently to adjourn); 'all in favor' was said.

budget_items.topic: Green Communities grant funding to date
budget_items.what_was_said: The green team has obtained a sizable amount of state money for energy upgrades; the goal of cutting energy use by a set percentage has not been met.
The town could apply for a quarter-million-dollar round next year for non-lighting energy projects such as heat pumps.
Projects must show a short payback, preferably four years or under, with longer allowed for long-lived equipment.
A state grant offers full funding for projects under a small total cost.
A bid for technical assistance and engineering design funds is due in November; the grant is capped at a stated amount.

budget_items.topic: Cost of audits vs. project budgets
budget_items.what_was_said: A facilities lead said money for an assessment would compete with other projects in the budget; the grant amount was discussed.
The committee has applied roughly every other year, and a cap on the amount applies before limits start.
A state training program on advanced building control systems costs a fee that grants can cover.
Past projects have received a large share of cost from the state.
The town got an incentive toward an electric cruiser.

budget_items.topic: Utility charge for street light infrastructure
budget_items.what_was_said: The utility charged for infrastructure that went unmaintained; the town has money to pay for rewiring regardless of any rebate.
Savings were cited from not using a consultant sooner, and a share of the utility bill was said to be maintenance.

budget_items.topic: Mini splits proposal for a building
budget_items.what_was_said: A building reuse committee was discussing a proposal for mini splits at a large dollar figure.
The task force suggested grants could fund pump motor replacements.
A past insulation project cost doubled with prevailing wage, so materials were bought and installed in-house.

decisions.decision: Agreed to compile a list of candidate facilities projects to map which to pursue next spring, next fall, or later.
A member will contact Mass Save about municipal building energy assessments and their cost.
Chair will introduce a utility contact for rebate questions and send resources and information to facilities staff.
Facilities staff will send a starter list of projects; the school side will share its list for a quick viability review.
Chair may ask for time at town meeting to recap street lights and the task force's work.

what_happened.line: The task force heard how to prepare for the next Green Communities grant round, expected next spring, and agreed that energy audits and a feasibility study with a short payback come first.
Facilities staff agreed to send a starter list of candidate projects, with the school side sharing its own list for a quick viability review.
A member will contact Mass Save about municipal building energy assessments and their cost, and the chair will introduce a utility contact on rebates.
The group reviewed the nearly finished LED street light project, including rewiring, dimming and a dispute with the utility over an infrastructure charge.
No formal votes were recorded; the result of a closing motion is not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: Green Communities grants pay for energy upgrades to town and school buildings, so the project list and audits decide which heat pump, boiler or rooftop unit work could be partly state-funded instead of coming from the town's capital budget.
Energy assessments would compete with other projects for money in the facilities budget, so whether the town pays for them may come up in budget season.
